origin.description: Convert character vector to ASCII, replacing non-ASCII characters with single-byte (\x00) or two-byte (\u0000) codes.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A character vector, possibly containing non-ASCII characters.

arguments.name: bytes
arguments.text: Either 1 or 2, for single-byte (\x00) or two-byte (\u0000) codes.

arguments.name: fallback
arguments.text: An output character to use when input characters cannot be converted.

origin.details: Each element is split into characters. ASCII stays as-is. One-byte mode writes \x hex for encodable bytes and uses fallback with a warning when a code point does not fit. Two-byte mode writes \u with four hex digits. To render single backslashes, write or cat the result to a file.
origin.value: A character vector like x, except non-ASCII characters have been replaced with \x00 or \u0000 codes.
origin.example:
cities <- c("S\u00e3o Paulo", "Reykjav\u00edk")
print(cities)
ASCIIfy(cities, 1)
ASCIIfy(cities, 2)

athens <- "\u0391\u03b8\u03ae\u03bd\u03b1"
print(athens)
ASCIIfy(athens)

translation.description: Convert character vector to ASCII, replacing non-ASCII characters with single-byte (\x00) or two-byte (\u0000) codes.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A string or sequence of strings, possibly containing non-ASCII characters.

arguments.name: bytes
arguments.text: Either 1 or 2, for single-byte (\x00) or two-byte (\u0000) codes.

arguments.name: fallback
arguments.text: An output character to use when input characters cannot be converted.

translation.details: Each element is split into Unicode characters. ASCII stays as-is. One-byte mode writes \x hex for encodable bytes and uses fallback with a warning when a code point does not fit. Two-byte mode writes \u with four hex digits. A single string returns a string; several strings return a list.
translation.value: A string or list of strings like x, except non-ASCII characters have been replaced with \x00 or \u0000 codes.
translation.example:
from gtools.asciiify import ASCIIfy
cities = ["S\u00e3o Paulo", "Reykjav\u00edk"]
print(cities)
print(ASCIIfy(cities, 1))
print(ASCIIfy(cities, 2))

athens = "\u0391\u03b8\u03ae\u03bd\u03b1"
print(athens)
print(ASCIIfy(athens))
